contract: OpenID Connect login/callback/logout/auto-redirect flow parity with upstream OpenIDAuthStrategy, including settings side effects.

invariants.contract: With authOpenIDAutoRegister on, an unknown provider subject creates exactly one active 'user' whose username is preferred_username and whose email is the verified email, stores authOpenIDSub in extraData and creates exactly one refreshable session. With auto-registration off, an unknown subject is denied with 302 /login?error=Unauthorized&autoLaunch=0 and creates no user or session. Two logins of the same subject reuse that user row (same id) and add one session each without a second user_added event.

When authOpenIDMatchExistingBy=email and userinfo.email_verified is not false, the callback matches an active existing user by email: the user keeps its id, username, email, type and every existing extraData member, gains extraData.authOpenIDSub = userinfo.sub, and gets exactly one session. When email_verified is explicitly false, when the userinfo carries no email, or when the matched user already has a different authOpenIDSub, the login is denied with the Unauthorized login redirect, links nothing and creates no session. When authOpenIDMatchExistingBy=username, the mode the web client offers, an unlinked user whose username equals the userinfo preferred_username is linked the same way and keeps its fields.
exceptions: JSON member order inside extraData is free; only membership and values are asserted.

invariants.contract: Successful OIDC auto-registration emits one user_added event with the legacy browser user shape (id, username, email, type, non-empty token, isActive, hasOpenIDLink true, permissions without librariesAccessible/itemTagsSelected, librariesAccessible/itemTagsSelected/mediaProgress/bookmarks arrays) to root/admin sockets and no user_added to an ordinary user socket.
exceptions: The full Socket.IO audience matrix for every user event is owned by the user_admin packet; this invariant asserts only the auto-registration event and the ordinary-user exclusion.

invariants.contract: A web OIDC callback whose ID token has a broken RS256 signature, a foreign issuer, a foreign audience or an expired exp answers 302 /login?error=Unauthorized&autoLaunch=0, creates no user or session and consumes the flow.
exceptions: The pinned strategy sends no nonce with response_type=code, so nonce validation cannot be exercised; signature, issuer, audience and exp are.

invariants.contract: A native start rejects an unlisted redirect_uri and a missing code_challenge with 400 and no credentials. A valid start binds the app's S256 challenge and a server-generated state: both appear in the provider URL, the mobile-redirect answer carries the provider code and that state to the app URI, and the mobile-redirect state is consumed once (a second use is 400) while the app callback with the same state still completes.

A web start sets HttpOnly auth_cb (Max-Age 600, value the callback URL), HttpOnly auth_method=openid (Max-Age 315360000) and a fresh connect.sid; the success callback sets an HttpOnly Path=/ refresh_token and a Secure SameSite=Strict openid_id_token, and the returned access token carries userId (the new user), username and type=access with a future exp.
exceptions: Opaque cookie values and the Express session implementation are free; the asserted fields are names, values that are URLs, Max-Age, Path, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite.

invariants.contract: A successful native exchange with the app's PKCE verifier returns the API login payload with non-empty accessToken and refreshToken, persists exactly one linked user and one session whose refreshToken equals the returned value, and refreshes. Replaying the consumed callback answers status 400 and creates no second user or session.
exceptions: Only the local RS256 stub, one allowlisted redirect URI, S256 and the auto-registration mode are covered.

invariants.contract: After a valid native authorization and mobile redirect, a callback with an incorrect PKCE verifier follows the upstream web failure branch: 302 to /login?error=Error in callback&autoLaunch=0, because the strategy stores the mobile redirect URI string in session.mobile while Auth.js compares it with true and the provider's invalid_grant is an error rather than a plain failure. It creates no provider-linked user or session and consumes the flow, so a replay returns status 400.
exceptions: The live v2.37.2 answer is 302 Error in callback, not the 302 Unauthorized recorded by an earlier differential: a provider token rejection propagates as an error to the Express error branch. The official app does not read this redirect.

invariants.contract: POST /logout carrying the refresh_token cookie, auth_method=openid and the openid_id_token cookie answers 200 {redirect_url:<configured end_session_endpoint>?id_token_hint=<that id_token>&post_logout_redirect_uri=<request origin>/audiobookshelf/login}, expires the refresh_token, auth_method and openid_id_token cookies, deletes the session row and keeps the linked user.
exceptions: The route itself is owned by route-r006 in the auth packet; this scenario proves the OIDC-specific end-session URL, id_token_hint and cookie interaction.

invariants.contract: A started web flow still completes after the same browser makes other requests with its session cookie; the flow is not bound to the start request. The Express store keeps sessions for 24 hours of inactivity; the exact boundary is not exercised.
exceptions: The 24-hour boundary and rolling session-touch renewal are not executable in a bounded run.

invariants.contract: The mobile redirect URI mapping is held in the strategy's LRU for ten minutes and each state is one-time; a consumed or never-issued state answers status 400 with no Location and no credentials.
exceptions: The exact ten-minute boundary is unexecuted because the timer is in-process with no API or clock injection; a not-held state produces the identical response.

invariants.contract: With authOpenIDGroupClaim=groups the provider scope includes that claim, a groups=[admin] login makes the linked user an admin, and a later groups=[user] login downgrades the same user to user while each login creates a session. A userinfo without the configured claim, or with a group outside admin/user/guest, is denied with the Unauthorized login redirect and creates no user or session. A root user matched by email is denied when the claim says user, and succeeds unchanged when it says admin.
exceptions: The root downgrade refusal is asserted through the denial and the admin-group success; the subject link upstream leaves behind before refusing is not asserted as contract (the scenario clears it with the unlink route).

invariants.contract: With authOpenIDAdvancedPermsClaim=abs_perms, a non-admin login whose claim sets canDownload=false and canAccessExplicitContent=false persists exactly those permission changes on the linked user (other defaults unchanged), which GET /api/me then reports. An admin matched by email keeps its permissions. A userinfo without the configured claim is denied with the Unauthorized login redirect, and the user row auto-registered moments earlier is removed again: no user with that subject and no session remains.

PATCH /api/users/:id/openid-unlink clears extraData.authOpenIDSub for that user so GET /api/me reports hasOpenIDLink false, while keeping the user and its sessions. A later OIDC login with the matching email links the same user again and adds one session.
exceptions: The unlink route (route-r077) and its user_updated event are owned by the user_admin packet; this scenario uses the call as the state change and asserts the OIDC re-link consequence.

invariants.contract: PATCH /api/auth-settings that removes openid from authActiveAuthMethods unregisters the provider strategy, so GET /status advertises only local; re-adding openid rebuilds the strategy from the current settings, GET /status advertises both methods again and a complete web login succeeds.
exceptions: The settings route itself is owned by the admin_settings packet; this scenario asserts the OIDC strategy registration and the client-read authMethods list.

invariants.contract: OpenID settings written through PATCH /api/auth-settings persist across a server restart: GET /api/auth-settings still returns the issuer, boot initialisation registers the provider strategy so GET /status still advertises openid, and a complete web login succeeds after the restart.

The auth_cb cookie lives 10 minutes while the browser session lasts 24 hours; when a valid provider callback arrives after auth_cb is gone, the server creates the linked user and one session and sets the refresh cookie, then answers 302 /login?error=No callback or already expired&autoLaunch=0 because no browser destination remains.
exceptions: The scenario omits the cookie instead of waiting ten minutes; the branch and its partial write are the same. The exact age boundary is not exercised.
force is not applicable: no OIDC operation in the pinned route contract has a force, override or refresh mode.
Exact 24-hour session expiry and the ten-minute mobile-redirect boundary are not executable; the shared scenarios assert every deterministic response around them.
The current shared scenarios replace the historical differential observations; the earlier reports remain provenance only.

Root users cannot be downgraded by the group claim, but upstream writes the subject link before refusing; the scenario asserts the denial and the admin-group login and clears the link instead of pinning that half-state.
